scope: Evidence for two diagnostics of the 40K stress project: (a) what is observable about player start-up from outside the process, and what the prepare actually spends its time on; (b) what replacing the nlohmann DOM dump in the canonical JSON writer changed, stage by stage, with a byte sweep proving the output text did not move. The 40K project is a deliberate stress case, not a capacity point: the only acceptance gate these numbers speak to is the R3 first-load clamp of 2000 ms, and even there the margin statement is a stress-case margin. Nothing here is a matrix row, a frontier point, or R3/R4 acceptance.

source_run.project: player-40k-project from the startup tree, archived verbatim under project/ (the chart gzipped): the runs' argv names the original path, so a re-run has to point the same file back at that path

runs.role: Probe start-up group: 6 processes untraced then 6 traced, 40000 entities, static.
runs.note: The batched order (six of one arm, then six of the other) cannot separate a trace effect from a drift in the machine, so this group is superseded by 20261101-a2 and its numbers are quoted only as the superseded attempt.

runs.role: Probe start-up group: 8 processes per arm, strictly alternating ABAB.
runs.note: The authoritative trace-perturbation test: the paired difference between traced and untraced is -0.23 %, well inside the 1 % gate the tabulator applies.

runs.role: Probe start-up group: entity ladder 1800/2400/2800/10000, traced, 3 processes per point.
runs.note: The entity-scaling check: prepare cost per entity is 43.48 us at 1800, 50.06 at 2400, 49.03 at 2800 and 51.42 at 10000, and 51.48 at 40000 taken from a2, a largest-over-smallest ratio of 1.184 against a 1.5 limit.  Three of the four arms sit at the same 50 us per entity, which is why the ladder is quoted as a ratio and not as a straight line.

runs.role: Before arm of the serializer comparison: 3 processes of the 40K project, PREPARE_TRACE on.
runs.note: Launched by watch_window.py with the label prefix writer-split-; the ad-hoc command line is not persisted, but every raw sample records its own argv, digest and environment.  prepare-cost/before/prepare-split.json is the summary over these logs.

runs.role: Watcher group: the player untraced x3 and traced x3, the probe untraced x1 and traced x1.
runs.note: Measures responsiveness from outside the process: time to window creation, to the first visible frame, and the probe-latency distribution of a thread that is not the renderer.  Also the group that shows the probe's own prepare scopes are the same 19 scopes in the same order as the probe of group a2.

runs.role: Watcher group: default order x3, device-first order x3, and one close-at-1s attempt each.
runs.note: The device-first order makes the window visible 2.09 s earlier and moves the first frame by +1.55 %, but the window is visible while not pumping, so four of the watcher's probes time out.  The close-at-1s pair shows a WM_CLOSE posted at 1.0 s is unreachable in the default order and takes 1.6893 s to act in the device-first order.

runs.role: Three single-process pilots of the traced player, default order.
runs.note: Instrument lineage and the [player.startup_phase] vocabulary come from here, and so does the player digest 56a04af4 that group w1's player arms report.  The first pilot was killed at the watcher's 25 s timeout with return code 1: it ran before the watcher could post a close, which is why the two later pilots exist.  Nothing is dropped for it.

runs.role: Two single-process pilots of the device-first patch.
runs.note: smoke-wf-01 is the threaded patch: return code 3221226505 (0xC0000409) from an off-thread destruction.  smoke-wf2-01 is the thread-free rewrite and exits 0.

runs.role: Watcher self-test: the same project launched six times, two plain runs, one dump run and three traced runs.
runs.note: Shows the trace vocabulary growing: trace-40k has no chart sub-scope, trace2 adds load_chart and load_canonical, trace3 adds json_dom_parse, chart_typed_read and chart_canonical_write.  That is the reason w1 has to be checked for the full 19 scopes instead of assuming any traced run speaks the same language.  No quoted number derives from this group, and it sits beside runs/ rather than inside it in the source tree.

runs.role: After arm of the serializer comparison: 3 processes, PREPARE_TRACE on, player cb575e15.
runs.note: Driven by run_prepare_split_set.py, which hashes the player before the first launch and after the last one and refuses to write the stamp if it moved, so this arm's digest is recorded by the instrument rather than inferred.

superseded_attempts.reason: summarise ran after the 03:34 rebuild, so it wrote the after binary's digest beside the before arm's numbers; the corrected stamp recovers the digest from the watcher's raw samples and the original is kept beside it

six untraced then six traced processes cannot separate a trace effect from drift; a2 alternates the arms per process and is what the report quotes.  The a group's numbers are printed as the superseded attempt, with its own over-limit spreads, rather than dropped

superseded_attempts.state: kept in full: one crashed pilot and one working pilot
superseded_attempts.reason: smoke-wf-01 is the threaded device-first patch and dies with 0xC0000409 because a single-threaded playback object is destroyed off-thread; smoke-wf2-01 is the thread-free rewrite.  Both are kept because the crash is why the design changed

superseded_notes: No group and no process was dropped, re-sampled or re-ordered.  Group a is the only superseded group, and it is archived in full with its over-limit spreads intact.
timer_runs and walks are empty on purpose: this archive contains no GPU-timer run and no stack walk, so the keys exist only to say so rather than to be absent.

Two probes and five player builds appear across these groups.  Their digests are in binding; no number is spliced across builds, and the only cross-build claim is about scope vocabulary, which was checked name by name in both directions.

The report's headline first-frame comparison uses the watcher for the before arm and the player's own [player.startup_phase] line for the after arm.  That is not a same-instrument difference and the report says so; both instruments are recorded here so the two numbers can be checked independently.

This archive tree was rebuilt from scratch several times before the copy beside this manifest passed both checks.  Two attempts aborted, one on the watcher self-test group living beside runs/ rather than inside it and one on a sweep record that carries no output field because eleven of the 22 corpus charts are v4 and the migrator cannot read them.  One attempt failed its own check: two digests were cited that nothing in the archive recorded, and the file count compared a set that included validation.json against one that could not.  One attempt passed its own check but failed the independent verifier, which objected that derived_files[] did not carry the content hash every copied file carries.  No measurement was repeated and no archive was patched in place: each rebuild re-read the same sources, and the four defects are recorded here rather than quietly repaired.

binding.head: 59e43daef283a1253a8689cc45e0252cd45a5681
binding.head_subject: Emit canonical JSON without a second value tree

probe.note: Three probe builds appear: the one groups a/a2/b measured is no longer on disk, the one w1 measured is also gone, and the on-disk binary was relinked by the serializer change.  The three differ in bytes but emit the same 19 prepare scopes in the same order, which is what makes their vocabulary comparable; their times are not comparable across builds.

player.note: The before arm's digest is recorded by the watcher in runs/20261101-c/raw/*.json and recovered by summarise; the after arm's is hashed by the runner before the first launch and after the last one.  before_arm_matches_after_original restates the provenance defect that the superseded stamp embodies: it bound the after-arm digest to the before-arm numbers, which is why it is not used for any difference.

serializer.note: The file the after arm measured; it did not exist before that commit.

canonical_40k.note: The 40000-entity case: the canonical text is 32 180 288 bytes and hashes to output_sha256 in both sweeps.  The three archived copies of those bytes (prepare-cost/before/40k-canonical.json.gz, before/work/...-t3.json.gz, after/work/...-t3.json.gz) must gunzip to that digest.

binding.tabulated_sha256_note: tabulated_sha256 is the archived copy, which is CRLF-normalised like every other text copy; tabulated_source_sha256 is the byte-exact file tabulate_startup.py wrote, and it is what a re-run has to reproduce.
binding.recorded_executables_note: Read out of the archived run records rather than typed in: each entry names the file that records the digest.  Several of these executables no longer exist on disk, and two of them (6938a31a..., the threaded start-up order that died with 0xC0000409, and 9da8939c..., the thread-free order that the w2 groups measured) are cited by the tabulation, which is why they are listed here instead of being left dangling.

environment.note: The watcher and the tabulator read wall clock through time.perf_counter; every timestamp in this archive is local wall clock and every mtime is converted to UTC only where the field name says _utc.
